How to set regional prices for software without losing money

If you sell software worldwide at one dollar price, you are priced out of every market where that dollar is a week of wages. Regional (purchasing-power, or PPP) pricing lets a developer in Lagos or Pune pay something that feels proportionate. Done carelessly it also gives away margin. This is how to do it carefully.

Why a discount can earn more

A copy of your software costs almost nothing to deliver. If a visitor would not buy at full price, any price above your support cost is extra revenue. The risk is the visitors who would have paid full price and now pay less. So the question is never "is it fair?" but "does it bring in enough extra buyers?"

The break-even rule

A discount of d only pays for itself if conversion rises by 1 ÷ (1 − d) − 1.

DiscountExtra conversion needed to break even
20%+25%
40%+67%
50%+100% (conversion doubles)
70%+233%

That is why deep discounts are a bet. They pay off where your current conversion in that country is close to zero because of price, and not where you already sell reasonably well.

Damp it, and set a floor

A country with a quarter of the US price level should not pay a quarter of the US price: local buyers are often professionals paid in dollars or employed by international companies. The strength setting raises the price level to a power below 1, so the discount is shallower than the raw gap. The floor keeps any price above a share of your base so support and payment fees still leave you something.

Keep the table small

Fifty different prices are hard to explain and easy to get wrong. Collapsing countries into three or four tiers gives you a table you can read at a glance and a handful of discount codes to maintain. The generator groups them by band and prints the countries for each discount.

Limit the abuse

  • Decide the price from the card's billing country or the store's storefront, not from an IP address.
  • Keep the gap between tiers modest, and the floor above what a VPN subscription is worth.
  • Do not advertise the cheap price on the full-price page.
  • Watch refunds and chargebacks by country before deepening a discount.

Taxes and currency

Tax is added on top of your price in many countries. Currency conversion and local price endings are best done by your payment processor or app store, so use the table for the dollar-equivalent target and let them localise it.

Try it

Put your base price into the generator, adjust strength and floor, and paste your own traffic mix to see the break-even conversion and a revenue what-if. It runs entirely in your browser.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is. General information about pricing strategy, not financial, tax or legal advice. The price levels used are rounded estimates and your own sales data should decide your prices. Optional support.

    3. What would it do to revenue? (optional)

    A what-if with one elasticity for every market. It ignores VPN or card-country arbitrage, refunds, and customers who would have paid full price anyway. It is not a forecast.

    Run it from the command line

    node cli.mjs 29 --tiers 4
node cli.mjs 49 --strength 0.6 --floor 0.4 --format csv
node cli.mjs 29 --traffic shares.txt --elasticity 1.5

    Get cli.mjs and ppp.mjs from the repo. Node 18+, no dependencies.

    Common questions

    What is purchasing-power (PPP) pricing?

    Charging customers in lower-cost countries less, so the price feels the same relative to local incomes and prices. Software has almost no per-customer cost, so a smaller price from someone who would otherwise not buy at all can still add revenue.

    How much should I discount for India, Brazil or Nigeria?

    It depends on your product, so treat any number as a starting point. A common approach is to discount in proportion to the local price level but damp it, so a country at a quarter of the US price level pays more than a quarter of the US price. The strength slider does that, and the floor stops you going too low.

    Will people use a VPN to get the cheaper price?

    Some will. Most processors and app stores decide the price from the billing country or card, which is harder to fake than an IP address. Keep the gap modest, stay above your floor, and check how many cheap-region sales come from cards issued elsewhere.

    Does a discount actually earn more money?

    Only if enough extra people buy. The page shows the extra conversion a discount must win just to break even: a 50% discount needs conversion to double. The revenue model lets you try an elasticity assumption against your own traffic mix; it is a what-if, not a forecast.

    Where do the price-level numbers come from?

    They are rounded estimates in the spirit of the World Bank International Comparison Program price levels, with the US at 100. They are not exact and they change. Paste your own index values to override any country before you publish a price.

    Does it convert to local currency?

    No. Prices are in the same currency as your base price. Converting at today's exchange rate and snapping to the currency's usual price points is best left to your payment processor or app store.

    Is anything uploaded?

    No. Everything runs in this page and the page makes no network calls.
